runConfig.positivePrompt: Static locked wide camera, one continuous five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame anatomy, identity, composition, lighting, and background reference. Exactly one Tyrannosaurus rex remains on the right bank and exactly one Triceratops horridus remains on the left bank, always separated by the open stream. The Triceratops remains completely motionless for the entire shot. The Tyrannosaurus torso, pelvis, hips, two planted hind feet, toes, two tiny two-fingered arms, and complete heavy tail remain motionless in exactly their source positions. Only the continuously attached Tyrannosaurus head, short muscular neck, throat, and lower jaw move. During the first second it holds still with its mouth closed. During the second second it makes one small controlled downward head nod of about five degrees without moving forward. It then lifts the head slightly while smoothly opening only the lower jaw to a natural twenty-five-degree gape and expanding the throat once as a silent roar. During the final second it holds the open-mouth display. It does not close the jaw, recoil, lunge, repeat, or reverse the motion. Preserve the deep broad side-profile skull, stable upper and lower tooth rows, low tongue, dark mouth interior, and uninterrupted neck attachment. Preserve the Triceratops two brow horns, one nasal horn, solid frill, four planted legs, and complete tail. No contact, attack, injury, or panic. Silent, non-graphic generated display hypothesis for ages five to fourteen.
